substeps.label: C5 · SEM, unetched: porosity first
substeps.caption: Into the SEM unetched: porosity is imaged before any etch, because etch pits look like pores. Backscattered electrons, about 100x, roughly six fields up each wall: about 250 fields for all 42 walls, so use the stage's automated tiling if the Apreo has it.
substeps.watch_out: image porosity before any etch: etch pits look like pores.

substeps.label: C5 · each wall's section
substeps.caption: Each wall's section, 1.27 mm wide, with its core band dashed: pores are counted only there, clear of the contours. (The pores here are drawn, not data.)

substeps.label: C4 · etch
substeps.caption: Then etch to bring out the melt-pool boundaries, straight after the final polish (316 passivates fast): for example 10 % oxalic acid electrolytically, or a short dip in a mixed-acid etch in the fume hood.
substeps.watch_out: etch straight after the final polish, and lightly: over-etching pits the surface.

substeps.label: C5 · back in: the last layer's pools
substeps.caption: Back into the SEM (or under the optical microscope) to image the top of each wall, where the last layer's pools were never remelted.

substeps.label: C6 · pool depth at the top
substeps.caption: The AM Module's steady-state pool is one of these arcs, if the hatch runs along the wall. If it runs across, the section shows only a flat fusion line, which gives the depth but not the width.
substeps.watch_out: if the hatch runs across the wall, the section gives depth but no width.
